label: early original-phase input of u/e/v/n/3/c (positions 1-2)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, at the 2nd-4th positions (t=1: 64% of mass, t=2: 30%, t=3: 5%), never at t=0 and almost never at the delimiter or during copying (<0.5% of mass). It responds to the current input token: u (33% of mass), e, v, n, then 3, c, q; other tokens rarely trigger it. Activations are largest at t=1 with in_tok u/e right after first tokens like b/d/v (top examples: b v [u], d v [u], d l v [u]). It is gated by context: the same token at t=1 is often silent after first tokens like r, y, i, g, a, and restricting prev_tok to a favourable set (v,d,j,n,c,3,b,e,q,1) raises dev F1 only to about 0.50. The predicate captures about 91% of activation mass on dev but has low precision (about 0.28), because whether it fires depends on the preceding hidden state in a way no simple token rule captures.
